maintenance_impact.evidence: Every handler implementor and the package's own doubles must now supply fabricated members; content-type and release duties are claimed both by the handler surface and the response pipeline (same-named methods, different fates), while entry docs teach a false requirement. Removal restores the exported extension contract and clear long-term responsibility ownership.

development_plausibility.evidence: The widening reads naturally as a 'uniform capability surface' refactor: idiomatic doc comments, promotion-based compatibility, an escape-hatch seam with a credible rationale, and updated docs and doubles. Slight tells remain — identically worded mirrored-interface comments in two packages and a public-contract break at odds with the repo's careful deprecation discipline.

prompt_accuracy.evidence: Names the declaration-vs-consumption mismatch, enumerates every affected surface (contract, seam, both consumers, three transports, docs, doubles), pins finished state per surface and the end-to-end preservation boundary, and explicitly rules out the costly near-miss of unifying response typing/release onto handlers plus any test weakening — decisively preventing wrong direction, incomplete cleanup, and irrelevant redesign.

semantic_diversity.evidence: Five purposes: purging fabricated members, relocating genuinely dispatched capabilities (InvokeStream, BaseContext) off the exported contract, re-plumbing consumers including restoring the deleted RPC fallback, trimming unexercised doubles, and doc syncing. Purge and relocation follow different rules; transport and double trims share one removal rule, so not every counted purpose needs its own decision.

localization_burden.evidence: Scope is named per area, but member-level decisions require combining dispatch flows across handler.go, invoke_loop, rpc_function, consumers and tests; InvokeStream's fate needs the loop's dispatch plus contract satisfiability. The solver must find the private invoker alias and exclude the pooled response type's same-named ContentType/Close, which have real consumers.

repair_coordination.evidence: Contract satisfiability interacts with behavior preservation: removing BaseContext forces simultaneous consumer re-plumbing, and restoring the modes' historically asymmetric base-context fallback must keep both execution modes correct. Doc re-sync has no compiler check; rewiring one consumer alone breaks compilation or silently diverges context-parent semantics.

mechanical_resistance.evidence: Deleting members with no dispatch sites uniformly fixes the transport widenings and forced stubs, but the dispatched InvokeStream/BaseContext relocation, invoker seam, consumer re-typing and doc restoration each need separate decisions — roughly a third of distinct repair spots, inside the 20–40% band.

behavioral_risk.evidence: Rewiring both consumers to identical direct reads while dropping only the RPC mode's nil-fallback compiles and passes configured-context calls, failing when no base context is set — special state. Silent incompleteness is possible (the seam or accessor could remain), though no second unchecked behavioral failure path is established from the supplied files.

recommendation_reason: Deterministic validation passed and every Quality dimension meets the retention threshold.
